payload.author: AceHack
payload.body:
## Context

Succession-infrastructure gap identified round 35. Scan every skill under `.claude/skills/`, every numbered section in `GOVERNANCE.md`, and every reviewer clause in `docs/CONFLICT-RESOLUTION.md` for the pattern "escalate to the human maintainer" / "binding decisions go via human". For each, check whether the *criteria the maintainer applies* are written down somewhere a successor could read.

Goal: every `escalate-to-human` path carries criteria a stranger could apply when the named human is unavailable. This closes the single largest will-propagation hole in the current factory.

## Proposed work

- Mechanical audit of `.claude/skills/**`, `GOVERNANCE.md`, and `docs/CONFLICT-RESOLUTION.md` for escalate-to-human patterns.
- For each hit, check if maintainer criteria are documented.
- Where not: draft criteria stubs or file the gap as a candidate ADR seed.
- Landing surface: `docs/research/escalation-criteria-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md` for audit output; individual ADRs for material criteria.
- Effort: M (audit is mechanical; criteria drafting is per-case and needs maintainer input for hard cases).

## Success signal

Every `escalate-to-human` path has readable criteria a successor could apply when the named human is unavailable.

## Source

- `docs/BACKLOG.md` L4409-L4425 (P1 — architectural hygiene)
- Round tag: round 35

## Reviewers

Aarav (audit), Kenji (Architect, criteria synthesis), maintainer (hard-case input)

## Context

The existing seven `skill-tune-up` ranking criteria (drift / contradiction / staleness / user-pain / bloat / best-practice-drift / portability-drift) do not cover the data-behaviour-mix violation class. Add mix-signature as criterion 8 with the same scoring rubric as the author-time prevention.

## Proposed work

- Add criterion 8 (mix-signature) to `skill-tune-up/SKILL.md`. Five signatures; threshold score >= 2 flags.
- Keep the seven existing criteria unchanged — criterion 8 is additive.
- Citation format: every flagged skill cites the mix signatures that triggered (e.g., "mix-signature: catalogue-section + what-survives-inventory").
- Finding feeds the `SPLIT` action (already in the closed action-set) via `skill-creator` execution.
- Routed through `skill-creator` workflow per `GOVERNANCE.md` §4 — no ad-hoc edits.

## Success signal

Next cadence fire of `skill-tune-up` surfaces mix-signature flags with citations; `SPLIT` action runs via `skill-creator`.

## Source

- `docs/BACKLOG.md` L4408 (P1 — architectural hygiene)

## Reviewers

skill-creator (to edit skill-tune-up/SKILL.md), Aarav (self-audit on next cadence)

payload.author: AceHack
payload.body:
## Context

FACTORY-HYGIENE row #51 cadenced detection (Aarav / skill-tune-up every 5-10 rounds) is the backstop; the author-time prevention lives in `skill-creator`'s workflow. Before a new skill lands, the workflow should score the draft against the five mix signatures and prompt for a three-surface split if score >= 2.

## Proposed work

- Add mix-signature scoring step to `skill-creator`'s authoring ritual.
- Signatures: gotcha-list > 3; worked-example > 20 lines; adapter/variants table; what-survives/breaks inventory; cross-platform matrix; plus catalog/catalogue/index/compendium/taxonomy keyword sections.
- If score >= 2, prompt for three-surface split: SKILL.md (behaviour) + `docs/<CAPITALIZED-NAME>.md` (data) + optional `docs/hygiene-history/<name>-history.md` (event log).
- Routed through `skill-creator` workflow per `GOVERNANCE.md` §4 — `skill-creator` self-modifies via canonical path.
- Checklist addition, not a rewrite.

## Success signal

New skills landing via `skill-creator` are scored at author-time; mixes are caught and split before landing rather than via cadenced retrospective sweep.

## Source

- `docs/BACKLOG.md` L4407 (P1 — architectural hygiene)

## Reviewers

skill-creator (self-modifies), Kenji (Architect)

## Context

1. `performance-analysis-expert` (642 lines; "Core background — the catalogue" ~130 lines + "Profiler-tool catalogue" ~80 lines)
2. `serialization-and-wire-format-expert` (478 lines; "Format catalogue" ~60 lines)
3. `compression-expert` (431 lines; "Core background" ~115 lines + "Hazards and anti-patterns" ~70 lines)
4. `hashing-expert` (415 lines; "Hash-function catalogue" ~75 lines + "Hazards — read these once, remember forever" ~55 lines)

Plus one borderline (`consent-ux-researcher`, single-catalog-in-otherwise-procedural) queued for next-cycle observation.

## Proposed work

- Routed through `skill-creator` workflow per `GOVERNANCE.md` §4 — no ad-hoc SKILL.md edits.
- Each split moves routine to SKILL.md (behaviour) and catalogue/background data to a new `docs/<CAPITALIZED-NAME>-REFERENCE.md`.
- No fire-history surface needed (these are expert-advice skills, not cadenced-fire routines).
- Priority order within the batch: `performance-analysis-expert` first (largest, most catalogue-heavy, highest invocation-context cost); others by line-count descending.

## Success signal

Four splits landed via `skill-creator`; cross-reference correctness verified; Aarav verifies post-split via next fire of row #51.

payload.author: AceHack
payload.body:
## Context

The durable-commit path needs copy-reduction work. The stated order: batching and group-commit first, then measure before reaching for direct/unbuffered I/O or other exotic modes. Measure-before-exotic is the discipline.

## Proposed work

- Implement batching and group-commit on the durable-commit path.
- Measure copy count and latency before considering direct/unbuffered I/O.
- Only escalate to exotic I/O modes if batching/group-commit measurements justify it.

## Success signal

## Context

Viktor's re-audit of commit `ce247a2` delivered a **NO verdict** on the "could I rebuild these modules from these specs alone?" gate. Third data-point breaks the two-ship unconditional-rebuild pattern that `operator-algebra` (Round 41) and `lsm-spine-family` (Round 42) established. Verdict preserved verbatim: *"Third data-point breaks the two-ship pattern. The pattern was convenient. The specs are not strong enough yet."*

## Proposed work

**Three P0s:**
- (1) `src/Core/NestedCircuit.fs:82,94-97` — cap-hit path sets `Converged = false` and still publishes `extract()` to parent. `operator-algebra/spec.md:486-488` forbids this. Fix: `IterateOp.StepAsync` raises `Result<_, DbspError>` or throws on cap-hit; plain `Nest` either removed or routed through the same failure path.
- (2) `src/Core/Primitive.fs:10-22` (DelayOp) and `src/Core/Recursive.fs:40-85` (FeedbackOp) — no `ClockStart` override; `state` / `initial` survives across outer ticks, breaking DBSP §5-6 inner-scope semantics. Add `ClockStart` override resetting per-scope state to declared initial.
- (3) Spec gap — no requirement states HOW strict operators observe "clean tick-0 semantics" on each outer tick. `operator-algebra/spec.md:420-423` says `ClockStart` **MAY** initialise per-scope state; must become **MUST**. Write a SHALL requirement.

**Six P1s:**
- (1) `src/Core/Circuit.fs:113-119` `Register` throws after `Build`; reconcile with `operator-algebra/spec.md:496-519` atomic-against-stepping topology mutation.
- (2) Implement async-replacement-waits-for-outstanding-tick-t continuations (`operator-algebra/spec.md:533-544`).
- (3) Document `NestedCircuit.fs:22-23,49` cap default `64` in `profiles/fsharp.md` per `circuit-recursion/spec.md:138-141`.
- (4) Reconcile cap-hit semantics: `circuit-recursion` allows passive-observable-handle read vs `operator-algebra` active-failure requirement.
- (5) Rewrite `operator-algebra/spec.md:420-421` MAY to MUST (root cause of P0-3).
- (6) Add `profiles/fsharp.md` entries for `NestedCircuit` / `IterateOp` / cap-default / `FeedbackOp`-to-requirement mapping.

**Three P2s:** complexity belongs in profile not base (`spec.md:615-625`); redundant "including under retractions" at `:549-555`; driver-is-linear classification (`circuit-recursion/spec.md:232-265`) lacks observable predicate.

## Success signal

Viktor re-audit of the follow-up returns **yes** on the rebuild-from-spec gate for `circuit-recursion` + `operator-algebra`.

## Context

Zeta currently uses CRC32C for checkpoint/payload integrity checks but has no authoritative document justifying that choice or laying out the future roadmap toward cryptographic hashing. Security reviewers (and downstream operators evaluating tamper-evidence properties) need a single source of truth that distinguishes the integrity-only guarantee CRC32C provides from the tamper-evident authentication guarantee SHA-256 would provide for checkpoint manifests.

The BACKLOG entry calls out the gap directly: the doc must justify CRC32C as integrity (not auth) and capture the future roadmap toward SHA-256 for tamper-evident checkpoint manifests. Absent this doc, crypto-choice is tribal knowledge and cannot be audited against SDL practice artifacts.

## Proposed work

- Create `docs/security/CRYPTO.md` as a new authoritative security doc.
- Document the current CRC32C usage sites and their threat model (integrity against accidental corruption, NOT authentication against a motivated adversary).
- Explain why CRC32C is sufficient for the current integrity scope (fast, well-understood collision properties for non-adversarial settings).
- Lay out the SHA-256 roadmap for tamper-evident checkpoint manifests, including which surfaces graduate when and what triggers the upgrade.
- Cross-link from relevant checkpoint/persistence docs and from the security SDL index.
- Per `GOVERNANCE.md §2`, edit `docs/` in-place (current-state-not-history).

## Success signal

`docs/security/CRYPTO.md` exists, justifies CRC32C as "integrity, not auth," and captures the "future roadmap for tamper-evident checkpoint manifests" using SHA-256. Row is checkable off in `docs/BACKLOG.md`.

## Source

- `docs/BACKLOG.md` L3501-L3503 (P0 — security / SDL artifacts)

## Reviewers

Nazar (security-operations-engineer), Aminata (threat-model-critic), Mateo (security-researcher), hashing-expert

## Context

The current `docs/security/THREAT-MODEL.md` is under-scoped for advanced-persistent-threat / nation-state and sophisticated supply-chain adversaries. Aaron (round-29 close) framed the gap directly:

> "in the real threat model we should take into consideration nation state and supply chain attacks."

Aaron's background is load-bearing on this work: he helped build the US smart grid (nation-state defense work) and is a gray hat with hardware side-channel experience. Treat APT + nation-state + sophisticated supply-chain as first-class threat classes, not box-ticks.

## Proposed work

- Revise `docs/security/THREAT-MODEL.md` adversary model: APT + nation-state + sophisticated supply-chain as first-class threat classes.
- Expand supply-chain coverage: package registries (NuGet, Mathlib, Homebrew formulae); build toolchain (dotnet SDK, elan, mise installers); CI runners (GitHub Actions runner image compromise, runner-level persistence); third-party actions (beyond SHA-pin mitigation); dep-graph attacks.
- For every mitigation, cite a real control (code / governance rule / CI gate / reviewer cadence). Unenforced mitigations become gap rows, not mitigation rows.
- Add side-channel + hardware adversary coverage: timing, cache behavior, microarchitectural leaks, speculative execution for tenant-isolated deployments.
- Author a nation-state response playbook covering compromise scenarios: `actions/checkout` compromise, `mise.run` hijack, poisoned NuGet package. Written before we need it.
- Complete `docs/security/THREAT-MODEL-SPACE-OPERA.md` as the serious-underneath-the-fun variant; every silly adversary maps to a real STRIDE class + real control + real CVE-style escalation path.

## Success signal

`docs/security/THREAT-MODEL.md` treats APT / nation-state / sophisticated supply-chain as first-class threat classes with every mitigation tied to a real enforced control; side-channel + hardware adversary classes present; response playbook lands before incident need; `THREAT-MODEL-SPACE-OPERA.md` complete with every adversary mapped to STRIDE + control + CVE-style escalation path.
